units: <cite ref="Ruth Rabbah 5:2">Ruth R. to II, 10</cite> (ref. to <he>להכירני</he>, <cite ref="Ruth Rabbah 5:2">ib.</cite>) <he>נתנבאה … להַכִּירָהּ כדרך וכ׳</he> she prophesied that he would know her in the way of all people (as his wife, cmp. <cite ref="J00106"><he>יָדַע</he></cite>).
<cite ref="Berakhot 10b:22">Ber. 10ᵇ</cite> <he>האשה מַכֶּרֶת באורחין וכ׳</he> woman recognizes the character of guests better than man.

<cite ref="Mishnah Rosh Hashanah 2:1">R. Hash. II, 1</cite> <he>אם אינן מַכִּירִין אותו</he> if the court does not know him personally. Y. Yeb. IV, 6ᵇ <he>כנסה ולא הִכִּירָהּ</he> he married her but did not touch her (v. supra).
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 7b:18">Snh. 7ᵇ</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Deuteronomy 1:17">Deut. I, 17</cite>) <he>לא תַכִּירֵהוּ</he> thou shalt not favor him (if he is thy friend); a. fr.—

<cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 9:23">Num. R. s. 9</cite> <he>במקום שמכיר</he> where he knows (the people), where he is acquainted; <cite ref="Sifrei Bamidbar 14:1">Sifré Num. 14</cite> <he>במקום שמכירין אותו</he>.

senses.gloss: to make known, identify; to acknowledge, own. R. Hash. l. c. מן המכירים on the declaration of those who identify (the witnesses; v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note 2).
units: <cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 43:7">Gen. R. s. 43</cite> <he>לא היה שמי ניכר … והִכַּרְתָּ אותי וכ׳</he> my name was unknown … and thou hast made me known among my creatures.

<cite ref="Sifrei Devarim 217">Sifré Deut. 217</cite>; <cite ref="Kiddushin 78b">Kidd. 78ᵇ</cite>, a. e. (ref. to <he>יכיר</he>, <cite ref="Deuteronomy 21:17">Deut. XXI, 17</cite>) <he>יַכִּירֶנּוּ לאחרים</he> he may identify him before others (as his first born son).
<cite ref="Sifrei Devarim 312:1">Sifré Deut. 312</cite> <he>שאהיה מַכִּירוֹ</he> that I may make it known as mine.
<cite ref="Sifrei Devarim 312:1">Ib.</cite> <he>מהיכן המקום מַכִּיר את חלקו</he> beginning with whom does the Lord acknowledge his share (claim as his)? With Jacob; a. fr.
<cite ref="Mishnah Kiddushin 3:5">Kidd. III, 5</cite> <he>ה׳ עוברה</he> her pregnancy was certain, v. <cite ref="E00521"><he>הַכָּרָה</he></cite>; <cite ref="Kiddushin 62b">ib. 62ᵇ</cite>.
<cite ref="Bava Metzia 93b">B. Mets. 93ᵇ</cite> <he>ה׳ הגנב</he> the thief was found out; a. e.
<cite ref="Berakhot 28a:9">Ber. 28ᵃ</cite> <he>מכותלי … אתה נ׳ וכ׳</he> by the walls of thy house, one sees that thou art a smith.
<cite ref="Kiddushin 31a:7">Kidd. 31ᵃ</cite> <he>מסוף דברך נ׳ וכ׳</he> from thy last words (the fifth and following commandments of the decalogue) it is seen that thy first one is true.
<cite ref="Kiddushin 31a:5">Ib.</cite> <he>מבין ריסי עיניך נ׳</he>, v. <cite ref="T00654"><he>רִיס</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Shabbat 91b:2">Sabb. 91ᵇ</cite> <he>מקומו נ׳</he> its location is discernible.
<cite ref="Sotah 9b:17">Sot. 9ᵇ</cite> <he>נִיכָּרִין דברי אמת</he> words of truth are easily recognized.
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 43:7">Gen. R. s. 43</cite>, v. supra; a. fr.

senses.gloss: to treat as a stranger, ignore; to discriminate against. Snh. l. c. (ref. to Deut. I, 17) לא תְנַכְּרֵהוּ (if he is thy enemy) do not discriminate against him (v. supra).
units: <cite ref="Sifrei Devarim 322:7">Sifré Deut. 322</cite> <he>בשעת … מְנַכְּרִים וכ׳</he> when Israel is in trouble, the nations ignore them and act as though they did not know them; a. e.
